_about: Tables for body/PHYSIOLOGY.md. Rendered into the doc and into body/data.js by body/build-body-data.py. Edit here, never in the doc. kind: science | history | model | fiction. mark: rex | proposed | open. conf: high | medium | low.

met.title: Energy cost of ship work (MET, multiples of resting metabolism)
met.source: Compendium of Physical Activities (Ainsworth et al.), standard reference; values are the nearest listed activity, not measured on sailors. PHY-MET
rows: Hauling lines, the capstan, pumping the bilge
heavy manual labour, shovelling / rowing vigorous

pal.title: Physical activity level (PAL) bands used for the day's total
pal.source: FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 energy requirements; PAL bands 1.2 to 2.4. PHY-FAO
rows: the top of the FAO band

sleep_debt.title: Sleep debt and what it does (model derived from Van Dongen et al. 2003)
sleep_debt.source: Van Dongen, Maislin, Mullington, Dinges, Sleep 26(2) 2003: 14 nights at 4 h matched 3 nights of total deprivation; cumulative wakefulness beyond about 15.84 h a day predicted lapses. PHY-VD
rows: yawning in dialogue; slower on the rigging
misses a line in the duty minigame; short with crew mates
nods off on watch (event); a crew mate says they look dead on their feet
equal to three nights without sleep: falls asleep standing; accident risk doubled

circadian.title: Time-of-day alertness (the circadian factor)
circadian.source: Two-process model (Borbely 1982); maritime watch studies find sleepiness peaks on the night and early-morning watches (Akerstedt et al. 2013; Colquhoun 1988). PHY-WATCH
rows: post-meal dip (the afternoon watch, where the Navy study found the worst vigilance)

wbgt_limits.title: Heat stress: WBGT ceilings for continuous work (acclimatised), and the model's core-temperature drift
wbgt_limits.source: NIOSH criteria (2016) and ACGIH TLVs as summarised by the US Navy heat-flag tables: light about 30 C, moderate about 28 C, heavy about 25 C WBGT for continuous acclimatised work; unacclimatised 1 to 2 C lower. PHY-WBGT
columns: Model: core drift above ceiling (C per hour per C over)

core_temp.title: Core temperature thresholds
core_temp.source: NIOSH: keep core under 38.0 C (95% of workers then under 39.2 C); heat stroke at about 40 C with CNS signs; hypothermia mild under 35 C, severe under 28 C (standard clinical thresholds). PHY-WBGT, PHY-COLD
rows: collapse; a MEDICINE.md condition; death risk per hour untreated
falls on deck, hot dry skin, raving
work capacity x0.6; sweat rate at max; hydration drains fast
pale, soaked, dizzy; asks to sit down
Dexterity x0.8 (numb hands), shivering costs energy
Dexterity x0.5, Wits x0.8; must be warmed

cold_water.title: Survival in the water (immersion), by water temperature
cold_water.source: Computational immersion study (PMC11234009): still fresh water 136/113/100 min at 5/2/0 C; static salt water 111/88/80/66 min at 5/2/0/-2 C. Boating-safety charts: under 15 min to exhaustion at 0 C, 1 to 2 h at 10 to 15 C, 2 to 12 h at 15 to 21 C, indefinite above about 26 C. Cold shock (gasp, loss of breathing control) worst at 10 to 15 C; drowning in the first minutes is the main killer. PHY-COLD
rows: never in the tropics; the Newfoundland fishery

hydration.title: Water balance thresholds (loss as % of body mass)
hydration.source: Sports Medicine 2015 supplement: hypohydration over 2% impairs aerobic work in warm-hot conditions, about 1% more per 1 C skin temperature above 27 C; sweat rates 0.5 to over 2.5 L/h in heat; total fluid need 3.7 L/day men, 2.7 women (US National Academies), 2 L drinking water (WHO). PHY-HYD
rows: Endurance x0.85 (x0.75 in heat); Wits x0.9; heat strain faster
Endurance x0.65; Strength x0.9; collapse risk in heat

banister.title: Cardiovascular fitness: the fitness-fatigue model constants
banister.source: Banister impulse-response model (Morton, Fitz-Clarke, Banister 1990): performance = base + k1*fitness - k2*fatigue, each an exponentially decaying sum of daily training loads. The 42-day / 7-day constants are the TrainingPeaks CTL/ATL convention, not a universal fit. PHY-BAN
rows: % per decade from the late 20s (sedentary); 5 to 7 trained

ageing.title: Ageing curves the body uses (the maximum, not the current value)
ageing.source: Grip strength pooled norms (Tomkinson et al. 2025, 2.4 million adults): peak at 30 to 39, faster decline from middle age; VO2max about -10% per decade from the late 20s; muscle mass -3 to -8% per decade after 30 with faster loss after 60 (sources disagree on the exact rate). PHY-AGE
rows: presbyopia: fine detail -20% by 50 (period: no spectacles at sea)
high tones first; -10% a decade after 50; gunners faster
Rex: skills never decrease, only rust

acclimatisation.title: Acclimatisation clocks
acclimatisation.source: Heat: plasma volume +9% after 6 days of exercise in humid heat, back to baseline about 25 days after stopping; full adaptation 10 to 14 days (PHY-HEATACC). Seasickness: 40% of 1,293 sailors affected, most mildly; 72% of cases in rough sea; incidence fell to 10% of its first-day value over 10 days at sea in cadets (PHY-SEA). Disease 'seasoning' is in MEDICINE.md.
rows: 10 to 14 days of work in heat
WBGT ceiling +2 C; sweat starts sooner; less salt lost per litre
nausea chance in a seaway x0.1 when habituated
small: shivering threshold lowered; not modelled beyond clothing
not relevant at sea; left out

recovery.title: What a night's sleep restores (the overnight tick)
recovery.source: Simplified from the subsystems: sleep repays debt hour for hour above need; muscle fatigue recovers by the 3CC R rate (MUSCULAR.md); glycogen refills from the day's carbohydrate (NUTRITION.md); wounds heal by phase (MEDICINE.md).
rows: debt -= max(0, hours slept - 8) ; debt += max(0, 8 - hours slept); a 4-on-4-off night counts 0.85 of its hours
resets to 0 after 7+ hours; otherwise carries (8 - slept)/8 of it
refills to its ceiling if slept, fed and watered; else to ceiling x (sleep x hydration x glycogen factors)
returns to 37.0 if sheltered; a wet cold night on deck lowers it (ENVIRONMENT)
both decay by their time constants; the day's load added
